title: Brihadisvara Temple, Thanjavur
summary: The Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, was built between 1003 and 1010 under the Chola king Rajaraja. It is a granite temple crowned by a thirteen-tier pyramidal vimana tower, called Dakshina Meru in its inscriptions. It forms part of UNESCO's Great Living Chola Temples.

uncertainty.note: ICOMOS: built from 1003 to 1010. UNESCO: inaugurated possibly in the 19th regal year (1003-1004 CE) and consecrated in the 25th (1009-1010 CE). End is the present.

when.display: Built 1003-1010 under Rajaraja I; standing today

reviewer_note: Shape stepped_pyramid for the 13-tier vimana. HEIGHT IS CONFLICTED: the ICOMOS evaluation (250bis) says the vimana is '65 m tall' and 'square in plan (30 x 30 m)'; UNESCO's property page says 'a height of 59.82 meters over the ground'. The model uses the ICOMOS pair, which comes from one page; the 30 m may describe a larger square than the tower's base proper. worldhistory.org (not used) says 63 m. Dates 1003-1010 are ICOMOS's; UNESCO's regnal-year dates match.
